title: Anthropic's $200M Gates Foundation Health Play
caption:
Anthropic just landed $200M from the Gates Foundation to tackle global health issues. But is Claude truly ready for the complexities of real-world medical data and diverse languages? This partnership signals a major shift, pushing LLMs into high-stakes environments where accuracy and accessibility are non-negotiable.

Learn how to build AI for impact, not just hype. Tap the link in bio and BUILD for the field guide.

slides.headline: $200M from Gates. Is Claude *really* ready for this?
slides.sub: The real challenge for LLMs in global health.

slides.title: The $200M Gates Foundation Pact
slides.body: Anthropic secured $200 million from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. The goal: accelerate AI for global health and development. This isn't just funding; it's a strategic vote of confidence in Claude's potential beyond chatbots.

slides.title: Where the $200M will *go*
bullets: Improve Claude's capabilities in low-resource languages.
Develop new AI tools for frontline health workers.
Focus on applications in maternal health, agriculture, and infectious disease.
slides.footer: Prioritizing accessibility and impact in underserved regions.

audiences.body: From remote clinics to research labs, AI tools aim to assist diagnosis, treatment, and data management in critical areas.
AI can accelerate drug discovery, vaccine development, and epidemiological modeling, potentially shortening response times to outbreaks.
The focus on low-resource languages and accessible tech could bring medical information and support to millions previously excluded.

slides.preStat: Despite the hype, AI in global health faces a steep curve. Just
slides.postStat: of healthcare organizations globally currently use AI in clinical settings.
slides.body: Data privacy, bias in models, and integration with existing infrastructure are massive hurdles. $200M is a start, not a solution.

slides.hook: Stop building AI for abstract problems.
